findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now uninstantiable
findings.body: After this change, MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler with an empty body (`pass`). StatefulDetectorHandler declares four abstract methods (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`) which the subclass does not implement. As a result, instantiating `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(detector)` raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...`. Previously the class inherited from `DetectorHandler` and provided a concrete stub `evaluate` that returned `[]`, so it could be instantiated and registered. Because `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, any code path that resolves the handler for this group type (now or once the feature is wired up) will fail. This is a behavior regression and should be fixed before merging, e.g. by keeping the stub `evaluate`, marking the class `NotImplementedError`-only, or using `# type: ignore[abstract]` along with an explicit raise.

findings.title: build_mock_occurrence_and_event called with wrong value for group_2
findings.body: In `test_state_results_multi_group`, the data packet has `"group_vals": {"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10}` but the mock for group_2 is built with `value=6` (`build_mock_occurrence_and_event(detector.detector_handler, "group_2", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`). The mock currently ignores the value parameter so the test passes, but the inconsistency masks a real bug if `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ever starts using `value` (e.g., to populate evidence_data). The test should pass `10` to match the data packet.

findings.title: build_mock_occurrence_and_event called with stale value=6 across tests
findings.body: `test_results_on_change` (line ~488) and `test_dedupe` (line ~508) call `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)` while their input data packets contain values `100` and `8` respectively. The mock does not use the value today, so the tests pass, but the inconsistency is the same kind of copy/paste mismatch as the one above and would silently desynchronize if the helper ever started using `value`. Pass the actual values from the data packet (100 and 8) for clarity and to keep the helper faithful.
